question: What is the meaning of supplier in relation to material information?
description: In the context of material information, a supplier is an entity that provides materials to other entities, such as manufacturers or remanufacturers. This can include information about material composition, hazardous substances, and recycled content. Suppliers consider a digital product passport a valuable platform for accessing data about recycled content, which can support quality and durability of remanufactured components. The supplier's role is crucial in the circular economy, as they can help track material lifecycle and provenance.

position is needed due to frequently occurring design changes and
chemical thresholds, as induced by changing regulation. Related to
this, suppliers consider a digital product passport a coveted platform

essential, this could support suppliers in securing the quality and dura-

This is summarised in Fig. 5. While material composition and a list of
hazardous substances are considered priority data, data about recycled
content is categorised as supportive. Despite being frequently men-
tioned as a point of awareness by suppliers, the external environment
is considered of little importance in this study, which is arguably caused
by the robustness of their respective components (e.g., casted alumin-
ium parts). Combined with low availability, external environment is
categorised as out of scope in the decision-making context of suppliers.

possible to link an instruction to its specific context. Some instructions 
may involve a step-by-step guide. The ‘Sequence’ pattern is selected to 
model the involved steps (see Fig. 5). 
With the Product module from Blomqvist et al. (2023), we are also 
able to create a detailed representation related to products, their com­
ponents, and compositions. It enables to model products manufactured 
in batches and specifying the amount of each component or material 
within a product. Our Product module has similar attributes and re­
lationships and we modeled it as a specialization of the Product module 
from Blomqvist et al. (2023) (see Fig. 6). 
All the above patterns selected for the Product module are combined 
and shown in supplementary information S4. The Schema diagram also 
shows some of the identified key notions that are directly linked to the 
Product module. 
4.3.3.1.2. Material. The term ‘resource’, as it is defined in ISO/DIS 
59004, is synonymous with “raw material”, “feedstock”, “material” or 
“component. In this context, the definition of resource is adopted for our 
‘Material’ key notion, which is an “asset from which a solution is created or 
implemented”. This standard defines solution as “product, service or a 
combination thereof, that fulfills a need”. We aligned our ‘Material’ key 
notion with the MAT's Material defined as “a homogeneous or inhomo­
geneous substance that can be used to form elements (physical products or 
their components.” Given the broad scope of the material definition we 
adopted from the ISO/DIS 59904, we introduced the mat:Material from 
MAT as a specialization of our ‘Material’ key notion. Table 7 provides the 
summary of how our ‘Material’ key notion aligns with Material from 
MAT. 
Following the IRs identified from literature and interviews, and the 
EC proposals for DPPs, the material module we introduced incorporates 
properties, relationships, and attributes associated with different types 
of materials. We started by first employing the ‘Name Stub’ and ‘Identi­
fier’ modules to identify materials by their names and unique identifiers 
(see Fig. 8). 
‘Explicit Typing’ pattern is selected to capture information related to 
the types or categories of materials such as metal, plastic or composite. 
This pattern allows for more straightforward classification and querying. 
It can also be used to categorize various types of material properties such 
as mechanical, chemical, etc., without the need to create a large number 
of subclasses (see Fig. 7). 
Tracking the lifecycle of materials is crucial for a circular economy. 
The ‘Provenance’ pattern enables to track materials by keeping record of 
their origin, how they have been treated and used, and where they end 
up. This is critical information for recycling or repurposing of materials. 
To capture the provenance information, we introduced the Material 
class as a specialized version of “EntityWithProvenance”. With this 
pattern, we can capture information about how the material is made 
using the ‘generatedBy’ property and who is responsible for the creating 
or manufacturing the material using the ‘attributedTo’ property. Using 
the ‘used’ property, we can indicate that something was utilized in the 
process of creating something else, in our case, what materials or com­
ponents were involved in making a final product. Additionally, the 
‘wasDerivedFrom’ makes it possible to model the historical context of 
materials by capturing information about from where or what the ma­
terial is originated from. The ‘AgentRole’ pattern also provides more 
context to model information related to agents and the roles they play to 
create and use materials along with the temporal information. Infor­
